Jukagirskij jazyk [The Yukaghir language]. Web entry dated 2020-10-30, arctic-megapedia.com/blog/2020/10/30/jukagirskij-jazyk/.
sources.note: Nothing on Chuvan phonology. The page's three 'ударение' occurrences are (i) a historiographic sentence that Jochelson 'дал ценные сведения о гармонии гласных и ударении' for living Yukaghir (no rule stated), (ii) the title of Krejnovich 1955 on 'логическое ударение', (iii) 'особые грамматические формы для выражения логического ударения' (focus). No акцент/тон hits. Living-Yukaghir vowel inventory (7 short, 6 long) is given, nothing prosodic even for the living languages.

sources.citation: Tailleur, Olivier Guy. 1959. Plaidoyer pour le youkaghir, branche orientale de la famille ouralienne. Lingua 8: 403-423. Amsterdam: North-Holland. [signed 'Helsinki, Olivier Guy Tailleur'; bibliography announces DTY = 'Le dialecte tchouvane du youkaghir, à paraître dans Orbis 9 (Louvain, 1960)', i.e. the paper that appeared as UAJb 34 (1962) 55-99.]
sources.note: No accent or stress remark of any kind (0 hits for accent/ccent/tonique/intonation/Betonung/stress in the 50,700-char article text; 'ton' hits are the possessive 'ton père'). The structural-trait list on pp.420-422 ('Contentons-nous ici de signaler les faits suivants') covers vowel harmony in two registers (labial / non-labial), traces of consonant alternation, -n ~ -d genitive alternation, verbo-nominal stems, invariable attributive adjective, predicative adjective = verb, personal pronouns as possessives - nothing prosodic. On Chuvan it says only that the eastern 'tchouvane' dialect is 'som…

sources.citation: Urmanchieva, A. Ju. (n.d., c.2022-2024). Чуванский язык [The Chuvan language]. In: Интерактивный атлас коренных малочисленных народов Севера, Сибири и Дальнего Востока: языки и культуры (atlaskmns.ru), section 'Чуванцы > Язык'. Online sketch: I. sociolinguistic data; II. linguistic data (II.1 classification, II.2 dialects, II.3 history of study with bibliography, II.4.1 phonetics: vocalism and consonantism, II.4.2 morphology, numerals, lexicon); III-IV resources. Covers extinct Chuvan (Benzing 1781 + Matjushkin 1821) and, separately, the Russian 'Markovo' dialect of the modern Chuvantsy.
sources.note: Section II.4.1 'Фонетика': records are fragmentary and pre-scientific, 'поэтому мы не можем составить точное представление о системе звуков чуванского языка'; tentatively five vowels a, e, e, o, u plus diphthongs (ei, uo); 'в имеющихся записях по чуванскому нет никаких специальных помет, которые отражали бы долготу гласных' (the records carry no marks reflecting vowel length); probable rounding harmony of suffix vowels (andre-le vs inemo-lo); consonant inventory not reconstructible, frequent sonorant+C clusters. No mention of word stress/accent for Chuvan at all (the only 'ударение' in the pa…

sources.note: Nothing; mentions Chuvan only as an 'Old Yukaghir' source siglum (OY Ch = Chuvan after Matjuškin) used by Dolgopolsky and Nikolaeva 2006.

sources.citation: Мудрак, О. А. 2010. [Рец. на:] Irina Nikolaeva. A Historical Dictionary of Yukaghir. Berlin - New York: Mouton de Gruyter, 2006. 500 pp. Вопросы языкового родства / Journal of Language Relationship 3: 164-173.
sources.note: No prosodic statement. Relevant by-product: the reviewer cites Benzing's 1781 Chuvan forms with their original Cyrillic diacritics and Nikolaeva's transliteration with acute accents, e.g. 'BO jṹgol῾ [юˆ´нголъ Бенсинга]', 'tṹdoĺẹ.. túδol῾ [ту´долѣ.. ту´долъ Бенсинг]', 'чуван. j-lẹ [юˆ´лѣ Бен]' - i.e. unlike Matjushkin's plain-Cyrillic list, the Benzing record (as edited by Tailleur 1962 / used in Nikolaeva 2006) carries accent-type marks on some words. This is wordlist-level marking only, with no statement of what the marks encode or where accent falls; it corrects the earlier reading's premis…

sources.citation: Seljutina, I. Ja. [2009]. Chuvanskij jazyk [The Chuvan language]. In: Istoricheskaja ènciklopedija Sibiri (ed. V. A. Lamin), online edition at Biblioteka sibirskogo kraevedenija (bsk.nios.ru/enciklodediya/chuvanskiy-yazyk); signed 'I. Ja. Seljutina'. Lit.: Matjushkin 1841, Tailleur 1962, LES 1990, Jazyki narodov Rossii: Krasnaja kniga 2002.
sources.note: No phonology content for the Yukaghiric idiom: sense 1 gives only classification (close to modern Upper Kolyma dialect; some consider it a separate language), period of use (17th - early 18th c.), area (Anadyr basin) and the corpus (22 phrases 1781 Benzing, 210 words Matjushkin; studied by O. Tailleur). The single phonetic remark in the entry ('Svoeobrazie fonetiki Ch. ja.. cokan'e') belongs to sense 2, the Russian-based speech of modern Chuvans.

sources.citation: Nikolaeva, I. A. & E. A. Xelimskij. 1997. Jukagirskij jazyk. In: Jazyki mira: Paleoaziatskie jazyki, 155-168. Moskva: Indrik.
sources.note: Stress rule (p.157, sec.2.1.2) is given only for modern Kolyma/Tundra Yukaghir. On Chuvan, p.155 and p.168 say only that Chuvan and Omok are 'izvestny tol'ko po fragmentarnym i vo mnogom defektnym zapisjam bolee chem polutoravekovoj davnosti' (known only from fragmentary, largely defective records more than 150 years old) and that, per Tailleur's processing, Chuvan is closer to Kolyma than to Tundra Yukaghir. Nothing on Chuvan stress.

sources.note: No phonology. 'a third dialect, Chuvan, was until recently spoken in the Anadyr river valley, but the last speakers of it died one to two decades ago, and the Chuvans are now completely russified' (refers to Burykin's atlas text for detail).

sources.citation: Schiefner, Anton. 1871. Beiträge zur Kenntniss der jukagirischen Sprache. Bulletin de l'Académie Impériale des Sciences de St.-Pétersbourg XVI (= Mélanges asiatiques VI: 409-446). St. Petersburg. [pp.436-437: 'Bacmeistersche Sprachproben (Boensing)' = the 22 Chuvan sentences sent by assessor Boensing to Pallas in 1781, printed in Latin transcription from L. Radloff's copy of the Adelung papers, with German translation.]
sources.note: No accent/stress remark anywhere in the Beiträge; the phonological paragraph ('In lautlicher Beziehung..', p.439-440) concerns absence of initial s and of f, aspirated x/kx, loss of final l - for Yukaghir generally. The Boensing text is printed almost without diacritics (scanned shows isolated circumflexes, e.g. 'nâxane'). The companion paper Schiefner 1871b (Maydell's Sprachproben, Mél; VI: 600-626, extract also kept) has an 'Accentbezeichnung' note (p.602) but it is about Maydell's Kolyma Yukaghir sentences, not Chuvan.
